findings.title: Meet fallback dereferences undefined destination calendar
findings.body: When evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, mainHostDestinationCalendar is undefined, but the code reads mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration unconditionally. Any Google Meet event without a destination calendar now throws a TypeError instead of falling back to Cal Video. Use optional chaining or check the main host destination before reading integration.

findings.title: Organization slug creation condition is inverted
findings.body: This changes the original !IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED slug condition to IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED. As a result, non-billing deployments create organizations without a slug, and billing-enabled deployments create a slug immediately instead of only storing requestedSlug. This is unrelated to destinationCalendar and breaks organization creation/routing.

findings.title: Non-Google calendar services still use only the first destination calendar
findings.body: EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents now calls createEvent once per destination calendar and passes the full multi-host CalendarEvent. GoogleCalendarService resolves the destination by credentialId, but Office365CalendarService still takes event.destinationCalendar[0] and builds /me/calendars/{first.externalId}/events using whichever credential is being processed. For a collective booking, the second host's Office365 credential can be used with the first host's calendar id, causing a 404 or creation in the wrong calendar. The same first-element logic remains in LarkCalendarService.createEvent and BaseCalendarService.createEvent, so the multi-host fix is incomplete for those integrations.

findings.title: Updated location references lose calendar credential and external id
findings.body: EventManager.updateLocation now builds references from result.externalId and result.credentialId, but CalendarManager.updateEvent's return value does not include either field. editLocation persists these references, so newly created BookingReferences have null credentialId and externalCalendarId. Future cancellation or reschedule then cannot identify the correct calendar credential/event. Add those fields in CalendarManager.updateEvent or derive them from the destination/credential being updated.

findings.title: Collective team destination calendars are dropped when main destination is null
findings.body: For a collective booking where neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar, evt.destinationCalendar is set to null. The following optional push is then skipped, so teamDestinationCalendars collected from other hosts is discarded. If only a non-organizer host has a connected calendar, that host receives no calendar event. Initialize destinationCalendar to [] when collecting team destinations.

findings.title: Google update/delete fallback compares externalId to itself
findings.body: When externalCalendarId is null or empty, this find compares cal.externalId to null/undefined, so selectedCalendar becomes undefined. The previous code fell back to event.destinationCalendar.externalId. Google update now calls events.update with calendarId undefined (error), and deleteEvent at line 317 falls back to primary, leaving the event on its actual non-primary destination calendar. Fall back to the first matching destination or the main host destination instead.

findings.title: Recurring collective cancellation still deletes only one calendar reference per booking
findings.body: The outer loop now iterates every booking calendar reference, but the recurring/allRemainingBookings branch still uses updBooking.references.find(...) and iterates only bookingToDelete.user.credentials. For a recurring collective booking with one calendar reference per host, only the first reference per booking is ever deleted, and the same deletion is repeated once per outer reference. Other hosts' calendar events remain. The inner logic must iterate all references and use each reference's credentialId.
